subject: Re: Post-demo recap + context-length profiling for pricing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + context-length profiling for pricing

Hi Sam / Priya
great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can produce an accurate pricing/POC plan:

1) Volume profile (monthly): please confirm typical and peak monthly token volumes (prompts vs completions). If you have a 3-month rolling average that's even better.
2) Context-length breakdown: for pricing we need approximate % of requests at 8k / 32k / 128k context windows and typical avg prompt tokens and avg completion tokens per request. For example: 60% are 8k w/avg prompt=300/avg completion=800, 30% 32k w/avg prompt=1,200/avg completion=2,000, 10% 128k for long retrievals.
3) Budget target / unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens you need us to hit for procurement to move forward? If you can share ballpark budget range that helps us propose the right dedicated vs hosted mix.
4) Sample prompts / a small corpus: we've attached a simple context-profiling-template.csv
if you can drop a handful of representative prompts (anonymized) we can run quick simulations to estimate effective tokens and KV cache reuse.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-math.xlsx (pricing scenarios), context-profiling-template.csv (sample schema), mutual-action-plan.pdf (draft).

Next steps: if you can reply with the items above by EOD Wednesday (3/18), Jordan and I will produce 2 pricing scenarios (hosted & dedicated) and a recommended rollout plan. Happy to jump on another quick call if it helps.

Thanks
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0189

On Mon, 16 Mar 2026 at 12:30 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote: (call notes attached)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + context-length profiling for pricing

Thanks Marissa
nice meeting you all. Answers inline below and high-level context: Acme AI is building an assistant + long-form summarization pipeline for enterprise customers; procurement is sensitive to $/1M token.

1) Volumes: current prod (pilot) = ~18M tokens/month (combined prompts + completions). Expected ramp to 120M tokens/month in 6-9 months if adoption goes well. Peak month last quarter was ~35M.

2) Context-length breakdown (rough estimates):
- 8k: 70% of requests (avg prompt tokens ~350, avg completion tokens ~700)
- 32k: 25% (these are longer documents & agent traces; avg prompt tokens ~2,000, avg completion ~2,500)
- 128k: 5% (rare analytics/archival summarization jobs; avg prompt tokens ~8,000, avg completion ~6,000)

3) Budget / unit economics: procurement is aiming for a target $10-12 per 1M tokens for hosted APIs. For dedicated/reserved pricing they'd consider higher committed spend if unit cost comes down to ~$6-8/1M tokens effective (accounting for reserved infra).

4) Sample data: attaching a small anonymized sample and we've filled the context-profiling-template.csv with 50 representative prompts.

Attached: sample_prompts.zip (sent via secure link), context-profiling-template.csv

Let us know if you need more granular breakdowns (by product vertical). Happy to hop on a technical call with Jordan.

Sam
Sam Patel, Head of Product
Acme AI
sam.patel@acme.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.ai>, Priya Reddy <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + context-length profiling for pricing

Thanks Sam
that's great detail and very helpful. A few quick clarifying questions so our cost models match your workload: 

- For the 32k requests (25%), are those typically single-shot generation over a single document, or do they represent multi-turn agent traces where the prompt includes conversation history + retrieval chunks?
- For the 128k batch jobs (5%), are these latency-tolerant (batch overnight) or do you have interactive SLAs? That impacts whether we propose reserved capacity vs on-demand.
- For the ramp plan to 120M/month, is that steady growth or concentrated in a few enterprise customers (i.e., bursty)?

Based on your target $10-12/1M hosted and $6-8/1M committed, initial back-of-envelope: at 120M/month hosted that would be roughly $1,200-1,440 / month per 1M? (note: typo: should be $1,200-1,440 total for 120M at $10-12/1M). We'll send a clearer per-scenario math sheet. Marissa - we'll prepare two scenarios (hosted API optimized with batching & caching, and a Dedicated reserved pool with committed throughput and quantization recommendations).

Proposed next step: technical sync Thurs 3/19 10:00 AM PT to walk setup & profiling outputs. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.ai>, Priya Reddy <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + context-length profiling for pricing

Thanks all - invite sent for Thurs 3/19 10:00 AM PT. Attached is a cleaned pricing scenarios sheet (redwood-pricing-math.xlsx) showing:

- Scenario A (Hosted + caching): per-1M effective token price assumptions and expected monthly cost at 18M / 35M / 120M tokens. Includes smart batching and KV caching that reduces billable tokens for repeated context.
- Scenario B (Dedicated reserved capacity): committed throughput assumptions, expected unit costs in the $6-8/1M range depending on commit term & quantization profile; includes fallback routing for peak bursts.

Action items: 
- Sam/Priya: confirm whether 32k requests are agent traces vs single-doc (Jordan question).
- Sam: confirm whether 128k jobs are latency-tolerant (batch) or interactive.
- Acme: if possible, share an export of token histograms (we can accept the CSV you filled).

I'll finalize the mutual action plan after the call and include a recommended pilot measurement (2-week profiling on a 1-2 GPU dedicated instance to validate unit economics).

Talk soon -
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
